actions.name: Create a threshold ECDSA key in the room
actions.summary: n members run a distributed key generation in the room. Each ends with a secret share; together they hold one ordinary secp256k1 public key, whose address on any chain looks single-sig. No one ever holds the whole key.

fields.name: parties
fields.means: the n members, each by their bound encryption identity (F-14), in an agreed index order (sorted public keys)

fields.name: t
fields.means: the threshold: how many shares must take part in signing

fields.name: curve
fields.means: secp256k1

fields.name: executionId
fields.means: a session id unique to this run

fields.name: engine
fields.means: the library and version that runs the protocol

fields.name: publicKey
fields.means: the joint public key, the ceremony's output

agreement.threshold: all n parties must complete the ceremony
agreement.domain: the engine's execution id; nothing is signed for any chain

requirements.name: mpc-party
requirements.target: a room member with a bound encryption identity (F-14) and a keystore that can hold a share

disclosure.field: broadcast round messages: commitments, public shares, proofs
unicast round messages, sealed to one recipient's encryption key (only that member can open them)
joint public key and the addresses derived from it

steps.does: proposes the parties, their indices, t, the engine and a fresh execution id
CGGMP engines first run auxiliary-info generation: each party makes Paillier moduli and zero-knowledge proofs (slow, prime generation); the output can be reused for later keys of the same group
steps.signs: nothing on any chain; each round message travels as a signed room log entry under the member's authorization key, which is the message authentication the libraries require

steps.does: the DKG: round 1 commits, round 2 opens the commitments and sends each party its share (sealed to that party), round 3 proves; every party checks every message and aborts on a bad one
steps.signs: nothing on any chain; each round message travels as a signed room log entry under the member's authorization key, which is the message authentication the libraries require

steps.does: each party stores its share in its own keystore; the joint public key is logged and the account is disclosed (S1) with its derived addresses (EVM: the last 20 bytes of keccak256 of the uncompressed key)

refusals.what: a round message that is not a signed log entry from the party it claims to come from
refusals.why: the libraries require every message to be authenticated; the room log's author signature is that authentication (invariant 4)

refusals.what: a unicast share sent under the room's epoch key instead of sealed to its one recipient
refusals.why: the libraries require point-to-point messages to be readable only by their recipient; the epoch key is shared by every member

refusals.what: an execution id that was used before
refusals.why: each protocol run needs a unique execution id so messages cannot be replayed from another run

refusals.what: a secret share, presignature or nonce written to the room log
refusals.why: invariant 4 and seam S7: secrets never enter the log; they live in each party's keystore

refusals.what: a party set or t that differs from what the proposal named, or an index order the parties do not share
refusals.why: invariant 1: the ceremony's inputs are the reviewed effect; all parties must agree on each other's indices

refusals.what: a share assigned because someone was admitted to the room
refusals.why: invariant 7: a key share is per person and comes only from a ceremony that names them, never from room admission

claims.claim: No single party ever holds the whole key, as long as fewer than t parties are corrupted.
The resulting address is an ordinary secp256k1 address; no chain can tell a group holds it.
A party who sends bad messages can stop the ceremony; with engines that lack identifiable abort (cggmp24), they are not named.
Each party must keep its share safe; losing more than n − t shares loses the key.

The engine is prototype-grade; before real funds the library is re-chosen for licence, CVE history and identifiable abort (no engine is built; the candidates are cggmp24 (LFDT-Lockness, formerly cggmp21), dkls23 (Silence Laboratories, non-commercial licence) and cb-mpc (Coinbase, MIT)).

evidence.what: CGGMP: UC non-interactive, proactive threshold ECDSA with identifiable aborts (the protocol family)
DKLs23: threshold ECDSA in three rounds, OT-based, dishonest majority
cggmp24 README: t-of-n keygen, (3+1)-round signing, aux-info generation; no key refresh and no identifiable abort; messages must be authenticated and p2p encrypted; unique execution ids
cggmp24 threshold keygen: Round1, Round2 (broadcast + unicast), Round3 messages
dkls23 library: DKG, DSG, refresh, quorum change; audit table
cb-mpc: DKG, refresh, derivation and signing; the application owns peer authentication and share storage

unverified: DKLs23 identifiable abort (carried from the registry).
Round count of the dkls23 and cb-mpc DKGs; the 3 above is cggmp24's threshold keygen.

actions.name: Send the native asset from a threshold ECDSA account
actions.summary: t of n share holders jointly sign one ordinary transaction that sends the chain's native asset from the key's address. EVM is the worked example; any chain that verifies secp256k1 ECDSA works the same way with its own digest.

fields.name: chain
fields.means: the CAIP-2 chain the transaction is for

fields.name: from
fields.means: the joint key's address on that chain

fields.name: to
fields.means: the payee's address

fields.name: value
fields.means: the amount, in the chain's base unit

fields.name: nonce
fields.means: the account's next nonce (EVM), read from the chain

fields.name: fees
fields.means: EVM: gasLimit, maxFeePerGas, maxPriorityFeePerGas

agreement.domain: the target chain's signing digest (EVM: the EIP-1559 type-2 signing hash, chain id included); CGGMP: 3 presign rounds + 1 online

requirements.name: fee
requirements.target: the key's address on the chain

disclosure.field: account address, nonce and balance reads
from (one ordinary address; the group is not visible)

steps.does: composes the effect; reads the account's nonce, balance and fees through the RPC (external reads); the room re-derives the chain's signing digest from the effect

reveals.field: account address, nonce and balance reads (RPC)

steps.does: t parties run presigning (CGGMP: 3 rounds, independent of the message); each keeps a one-time presignature in its keystore, marked consumed before it is used
steps.signs: nothing on any chain; each round message travels as a signed room log entry under the member's authorization key, which is the message authentication the libraries require

steps.does: each of the t parties re-derives the digest from the effect and issues its partial signature over it (the online round)
steps.signs: a partial ECDSA signature share over the transaction's signing digest (EVM: keccak256(0x02 || rlp([chainId, nonce, maxPriorityFeePerGas, maxFeePerGas, gasLimit, to, value, "", []])))

steps.does: any party combines t partials into one (r, s, v) signature, checks it against the joint public key, and broadcasts the signed transaction through its RPC
steps.signs: nothing new; the combined signature is an ordinary single ECDSA signature

steps.does: watches the transaction reach the chain's finality

refusals.what: a partial signature over a digest that is not the one the room re-derives from the effect
refusals.why: invariant 1 (F-4); and CVE-2025-66017: signing a bare hash from a presignature enabled forgery, so the digest is always derived from the effect, never accepted as input

refusals.what: using a presignature twice
refusals.why: reusing a presignature for two messages leaks the key; seam S7 marks it consumed in the keystore before the partial is released

refusals.what: a transaction that names no chain id (a legacy transaction without EIP-155), or whose chain id differs from the disclosed account's environment
refusals.why: invariant 2: the chain's own binding (EVM: the EIP-155 chain id in the signed transaction) must name the room's network

refusals.what: a stale nonce: the account's nonce moved since the proposal, re-read at review and at settle
refusals.why: invariant 10: the nonce is an external read that reached the digest

refusals.what: a signing session with other than t parties, or a party that does not hold a share of this key
refusals.why: invariant 9: every contributor is named; the engines require exactly t signers with their keygen indices

claims.claim: The chain sees one ordinary signature and cannot tell that a group signed, or which members did.
Any t share holders together can sign any transaction; the chain cannot check the room's policy.
The RPC provider sees the signed transaction before the mempool.
On EVM a signed transaction never expires; to cancel it, use the same nonce for another transaction. An Ed25519 target such as Solana forces expiry through its recent blockhash.
Chain binding is the target chain's own: explicit on EVM through the EIP-155 chain id.
With engines that lack identifiable abort (cggmp24), one party can stall signing without being named.

evidence.what: CGGMP: presigning independent of the message, then one online round
cggmp24 README: exactly t signers with their keygen indices; never reuse presignatures
CVE-2025-66017 (GHSA-8frv-q972-9rq5): altered presignatures and raw-hash signing allowed forgery in cggmp21 ≤ 0.6.3; fixed in cggmp24 0.7.0-alpha.2
EIP-1559: the type-2 transaction and its signing hash keccak256(0x02 || rlp([chainId, nonce, maxPriorityFeePerGas, maxFeePerGas, gasLimit, to, value, data, accessList]))
EIP-155: the chain id in the signed transaction
BIP-143: a non-EVM example of a chain signing digest (segwit v0 sighash), which the same key could sign

unverified: DKLs23 identifiable abort (carried from the registry).

actions.name: Refresh the shares of a threshold ECDSA key
actions.summary: The same parties run a ceremony that replaces every share with a new one for the same key. The address and threshold stay. Old shares become useless only once every party deletes theirs.

fields.name: publicKey
fields.means: the joint key whose shares are refreshed (unchanged)

fields.name: parties
fields.means: the same n parties and indices

fields.name: t
fields.means: unchanged

fields.name: executionId
fields.means: a session id unique to this run

fields.name: engine
fields.means: an engine with refresh: dkls23 (audited) or cb-mpc; cggmp24 has none

agreement.domain: the engine's execution id; nothing is signed for any chain

disclosure.field: broadcast round messages: commitments, public shares, proofs
unicast round messages, sealed to one recipient's encryption key (only that member can open them)
confirmation that the joint public key is unchanged

steps.does: proposes a refresh of the named key with a fresh execution id
the parties run the engine's refresh protocol (dkls23 reuses its keygen protocol with the existing shares as input)
steps.signs: nothing on any chain; each round message travels as a signed room log entry under the member's authorization key, which is the message authentication the libraries require

steps.does: each party checks the joint public key is unchanged, stores the new share, and deletes the old one

refusals.what: a round message that is not a signed log entry from the party it claims to come from
refusals.why: the libraries require every message to be authenticated; the room log's author signature is that authentication (invariant 4)

refusals.what: a unicast share sent under the room's epoch key instead of sealed to its one recipient
refusals.why: the libraries require point-to-point messages to be readable only by their recipient; the epoch key is shared by every member

refusals.what: an execution id that was used before
refusals.why: each protocol run needs a unique execution id so messages cannot be replayed from another run

refusals.what: a secret share, presignature or nonce written to the room log
refusals.why: invariant 4 and seam S7: secrets never enter the log; they live in each party's keystore

refusals.what: a refresh whose output public key differs from the input key
refusals.why: invariant 1: the effect names the key; a different key is a different account

refusals.what: signing with a share from before the refresh
refusals.why: old and new shares do not combine; the keystore retires the old share when the refresh completes

claims.claim: The address and the key stay the same.
Old shares are harmless only once every party deletes theirs; an attacker who gathered t old shares can still sign.

evidence.what: CGGMP: a periodic refresh mechanism gives proactive security
dkls23 key_refresh.rs: refresh existing shares without changing the public key; can recover lost shares
cb-mpc: refresh* APIs give fresh shares for the same key; a new key means a new dkg and migration
cggmp24 README: key refresh is not supported for threshold or non-threshold keys

unverified: Round count of refresh in dkls23 and cb-mpc; 3 is assumed from the keygen it reuses.

actions.name: Change the signers or threshold of a threshold ECDSA key
actions.summary: Old share holders and new parties run a ceremony that gives a new party set its own shares of the same key, possibly with a new threshold. The address stays; this is how signers change in this family.

fields.name: publicKey
fields.means: the joint key (unchanged)

fields.name: oldParties
fields.means: the current share holders taking part (at least t_old)

fields.name: newParties
fields.means: the new party set, each by bound encryption identity

fields.name: newT
fields.means: the new threshold

fields.name: executionId
fields.means: a session id unique to this run

fields.name: engine
fields.means: an engine with quorum change: dkls23 (not audited)

agreement.threshold: t_old of the old parties and all new parties
agreement.domain: the engine's execution id; nothing is signed for any chain

requirements.name: mpc-party
requirements.target: each new party's bound encryption identity

disclosure.field: broadcast round messages: commitments, public shares, proofs
unicast round messages, sealed to one recipient's encryption key (only that member can open them)
the new party set and threshold
confirmation that the joint public key is unchanged

steps.does: proposes the new party set and threshold for the named key
old share holders and new parties run the engine's quorum-change protocol; each new party receives a share sealed to it
steps.signs: nothing on any chain; each round message travels as a signed room log entry under the member's authorization key, which is the message authentication the libraries require

steps.does: every new party checks the joint public key is unchanged and stores its share; old parties delete theirs

refusals.what: a round message that is not a signed log entry from the party it claims to come from
refusals.why: the libraries require every message to be authenticated; the room log's author signature is that authentication (invariant 4)

refusals.what: a unicast share sent under the room's epoch key instead of sealed to its one recipient
refusals.why: the libraries require point-to-point messages to be readable only by their recipient; the epoch key is shared by every member

refusals.what: an execution id that was used before
refusals.why: each protocol run needs a unique execution id so messages cannot be replayed from another run

refusals.what: a secret share, presignature or nonce written to the room log
refusals.why: invariant 4 and seam S7: secrets never enter the log; they live in each party's keystore

refusals.what: a new threshold of 0 or above the new party count
refusals.why: a threshold no party set can meet locks the key

refusals.what: giving a share to someone because they were admitted to the room
refusals.why: invariant 7: a share is per person and comes only from a ceremony that names them

refusals.what: an output public key that differs from the input key
refusals.why: invariant 1: the effect names the key

claims.claim: The address stays the same when the signers change.
A removed party's old share still signs together with t_old − 1 other old shares until those are deleted; resharing does not revoke on its own.
No chain ever learns that the signers changed.

Of the three named libraries, only dkls23 implements a quorum change (same key, new signers), and its README lists that code as not audited (its refresh is audited); cggmp24 has no refresh or reshare. Whether cb-mpc can is unverified.
claims.party: the dkls23 quorum-change implementation (Silence Laboratories), which no audit covers

evidence.what: dkls23 README: quorum change adds or removes participants; its audit table marks quorum change as not audited
dkls23 quorum_change.rs: the quorum-change protocol
dkls23 is under the Silence Laboratories non-commercial licence
CGGMP: proactive refresh (same party set), the base the registry's reshare row builds on
dkls23 feature table: DKG, DSG and Refresh audited; Import, Export, Quorum Change and Migration not audited

unverified: Whether cb-mpc can move a key to a new party set without a new DKG.
Round count of dkls23 quorum change; 3 is assumed.
